channel.title: Grok Bot Changelog
channel.description: New features, improvements, and fixes in each Grok Bot release

item.title: Auto-review rule cards and smarter connectors (0.75.8)
item.description: New In the app, a Bot can offer to add, change, or remove one of your Auto-review rules on a card you confirm. 0.75.2+ Requires Grok Bot 0.75.2 or later Improved Auto-review takes a second look before showing an approval card, so fewer safe actions need one. A Bot's status line shows up right after you send, even for quick replies. When background work finishes, the Bot completes what you asked, including steps you said to take once it was done, and says what it would do next instead of acting on its own or on another agent's approval. 0.75.2+ Requires Grok Bot 0.75.2 or later Auto-review no longer counts a Bot saving or editing one of its routines as risky by itself. Auto-review approval cards in Slack describe the action, as they do in the app. Scheduling uses the calendar you've connected, Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar, and offers to connect one only when neither is. In a chat only you can see, a Bot reads your own private files without asking first. When a Bot installs a plugin while working, it can use the plugin's skills right away. People not on a Team Bot's share list, including teammates, no longer have access to it until an owner shares it with them. Teams Fixed When a connector such as X adds tools or fields, Bots can use them without you reconnecting it. A connector whose sign-in expired shows Authenticate in the app instead of Connected, matching what the Bot says. 0.71.2+ Requires Grok Bot 0.71.2 or later Images a connector returns as files reach the Bot as images, and other binary files are no longer read as garbled text. X Money connects in one tap for more X accounts, and if it can't connect yours, the Bot says so instead of offering a sign-in. When a Bot posts to Slack for you, such as from a routine, your phone isn't notified and its unread badge doesn't go up. In Slack, when a safety check blocks a Bot's reply, the Bot says so and suggests trying a different message. For most accounts, with Route traffic through this computer on, the connection comes back as soon as the Bot's computer wakes. A Team Bot's routines can read Slack channels you and the Bot are both in, instead of refusing every read. Teams When a Team Bot edits one of its own Slack messages, the message shows a muted (edited) label. Teams

item.title: Vault, email forwarding, and fewer approval cards (0.75.5)
item.description: New Bots can save your logins, cards, and contact info to a Vault in Settings and fill them in to sign in or check out. 0.75.2+ Requires Grok Bot 0.75.2 or later Bots can forward an email from their own inbox with its original formatting, images, and attachments. 0.75.2+ Requires Grok Bot 0.75.2 or later Bots record who asked for each message they post in Slack, so anyone in the thread can ask who requested it. For Halloween, you can give a Bot a pumpkin shape when you create it or change its avatar. 0.75.2+ Requires Grok Bot 0.75.2 or later Improved Auto-review asks less often for an action you asked for in your own words. After you deny an approval card, the Bot stops and doesn't try that action again until you send another message. Emails and Slack messages you ask a Bot to send go out once Auto-review allows them, while sends on routine and other turns still wait as drafts. When the Bot hands you its computer to sign in to a site that has a connector, it also offers that connector's connect card. Asking a Bot about your X account connects X through your linked X account, even if you removed the X plugin. Connecting X also connects X Money through the same account, and asking about your X Money balance, activity, or card installs X Money. Your routines can run up to 300 times an hour in total instead of 100, and each routine up to 200 times. With Route traffic through this computer on, Settings shows how many sites were blocked because they resolve to a private or VPN address. Teammates in their own DM with a Team Bot can react to messages, quote with Add to chat, and answer cards. Teams Team Bots name connectors as your plugin list does, such as Google Slides, when they ask to use one or say whose they used. Teams If your Grok Business seat doesn't cover Grok Bot yet, the usage limit message says to ask your Grok Business admin to connect your team. Fixed Auto-review falls back to an approval card less often, retrying a check that fails and reviewing long chats instead of stopping. Auto-review no longer waves through an action your request said to stop before, such as sending a message you asked only to draft. Asking a Bot about your X followers gets a plain answer that X doesn't offer it, instead of a browser sign-in to X. After an account merge, you keep managing the Bots you created and can share them with your team. Plugins with several servers, such as Salesforce, show each server as its own row, so you can see and sign in to every one. In Slack, Bots answer thread replies that were also sent to the channel, as they do other thread replies. On a Team Bot's Share this Bot card, someone who manages the Bot through a group sees their role as Manager. Teams Work a Team Bot hands off in a shared chat can use the connectors you allowed, and its reply says whose connector it used. Teams When a Team Bot's routine replies in a Slack thread, the Bot follows the thread and answers later replies without an @mention. Teams After you reset a chat whose first message was blocked, new messages get replies instead of an error.

item.title: Pages, new chat cards, and video creation (0.75.2)
item.description: New Bots can build Pages, such as reports, memos, and dashboards, that you edit together or have the Bot keep up to date. Bots can create videos from a description or from an image you share. You can pin Library pages, files, and links to a Pinned section that stays at the top and syncs across your devices. The dashboard's Pages section lists the Pages you've shared, where you can unshare or delete them. Hovering over or focusing a Library row shows a preview with who sent the item, when, and who can see a Page. Bots can pay with Shop Pay, through Shop checkout where a store accepts it and with a one-time Shop card elsewhere. You can connect X Money in one tap from a chat, the connector page, or checkout, after signing in to X if no X account is linked. Page owners can share a Page with their whole organization or with another team in it. Teams Team admins can limit who can share Pages with everyone on the team. Teams Team admins can turn on link previews that show a Team Bot's name, description, color, and shape wherever its link is posted. Teams A keyboard shortcuts sheet opens with ⌘/ and from Help, the profile menu, and the command palette. Typing > at the start of a composer line starts a block quote, and Backspace at the start of a quoted line lifts it back out. You can reorder attachments in the composer by dragging them or by pressing Alt with the arrow keys. You can connect Zoho CRM and choose your account's regional data center before you sign in. Team admins can upload a team icon, shown in workspace selectors and on Team Bots. Teams Team Bot owners and managers can let collaborators create routines from Configure. Teams Pages can capture the pointer and fill the screen. The GitHub connector can list your repositories, compare commits, list a pull request's commits, and read branch and issue comments. The built-in Gmail connection can attach files to drafts and sends, reply all, add a note when forwarding, and set label colors. Bots can create, update, or delete several Google Calendar events in one step, and edited events no longer shift to a different time. Routines can read the Bot's inboxes. A task the Bot hands off can create images and videos for the chat. A shared Team Bot's welcome in a team or group chat includes a Chat with me link, and an owner-only Bot greets only its owner. Teams Enterprise team admins can permanently delete a member's Grok Bot data from Manage Member Computers and Data in Security & Compliance, or through the Admin API. Enterprise Improved Cards in chat have a new design, from approvals and questions to files, links, and tables. The Bot details pane is one column, with a profile you click to edit above Media, Computer, and Routines tabs. Voice calls can draw on your earlier calls and recent chat with the Bot. The Bot opens links before sending them and leaves out broken ones. Auto-review approval cards describe the action in one sentence, name the app with its logo, and flag irreversible or sensitive changes. When you name a service, the Bot shows that connector's connect card in its first reply. When a connector signs you out or rejects a sign-in, the Bot says why, such as a restricted Google account, and how to fix it. When a routine hits a signed-out connector, the chat shows that connector's Reconnect card, at most once a day. Before a browser or desktop task that takes a few minutes, the Bot tells you it will take a while. If you already shared a password or code in the chat, the Bot uses it instead of refusing to continue. Pull requests, issues, and repositories mentioned in replies are links. When the Bot asks how to pay, you choose on a card. What a personal Bot saves to memory in one chat is remembered in all your chats with it, and only you can change it. Deleting a Bot permanently erases its conversations, memory, routines, and attachments, and removes its Slack app. The first email a Bot sends to someone new includes a one-click unsubscribe link. In Slack, asking the Bot to investigate, research, or check something gets a researched answer instead of a quick reply. Deleting your account first lists what you'd lose, and linking an already unified Grok account offers to merge into it instead of failing. Source links in replies show as compact citation chips, and company names as ticker pills. Number columns in chat tables line up on the decimal point, with header sublines, summary rows, and footnotes. Files you send show as cards with their type, name, and size, and captioned images offer Copy and Download on hover. Your reactions show the moment you tap them, and the message no longer shifts under your pointer. The Library opens faster for people with many Team Bots. Team Bots shared with you open straight to their saved conversation. Teams Browser sign-in waits up to 20 minutes and offers Copy link, and Reopen link resumes the same sign-in instead of starting over. Connect Apps shows each plugin's own logo, and setting up a plugin with your own OAuth client lists the callback URLs to register. A webhook routine's menu shows its URL and key, and the key stays hidden until you reveal it. Fixed Scrolling back quickly through a long chat no longer stalls before older messages load. Search results from further back in a chat open on the right message, even right after launch. Desktop notifications show Bot replies as plain text with full links, and skip replies you already read on another device. Voice calls survive network drops and crashes, pick your microphone back up when it reconnects, and the Bot can answer while you're muted. Pressing Enter once while recording a voice note sends it. Keyboard shortcuts, including ⌘F and the command palette, work while a Page is open, and the palette no longer closes the Page. Pressing Back while a Page is open closes the Page and stays on its Bot, instead of jumping to the Bot you viewed before. A Page's Share menu shows its current visibility, even after it changed on another device or the dashboard. When a message can't be saved, the app says whether your computer is out of disk space. The desktop app connects directly unless you've turned on a system proxy, which fixes loading behind some corporate proxies. When sign-in can't connect, the app asks you to check your connection instead of saying it stopped waiting for your browser. A new or reinstalled desktop app skips onboarding for an account that already finished it. Typing a follow-up leaves an open question card unanswered instead of answering it. Bot names mentioned with @ in a reply open that Bot's chat. Turning a Bot's tool on or off applies the state you saw, so an outdated list can't turn a blocked tool back on. When creating a Bot or publishing a Bot template is refused, the app shows the reason. Page cards and titles update as soon as the Bot renames a Page, and older Page cards open its latest version. Connect Apps waits longer for your plugins instead of showing Couldn't refresh, and built-in plugins no longer offer an Uninstall that failed. Buying credits, turning on auto top-up, and saving a spend limit show a confirmation or an error in the desktop app. Reactions and card answers you add while a Bot is working stay after its turn ends. An approval you don't answer in time leaves a chat line that names what expired. Large Google Slides edits update the live deck. Emails a Bot sends through Gmail show your name and the signature saved for that address, and reply drafts stay in their thread. Bot pictures larger than about 3 MB now save. A routine's result still reaches you if you send a message before the Bot finishes handing it off. Pausing and resuming a routine keeps your last choice, even when you tap from two devices. After an account merge, the remaining account keeps its Grok Bot email inbox and connector settings.

item.title: Smarter notifications and larger file attachments (0.71.2)
item.description: New Bots can send from a tagged form of their email address, like name+shop@, and a routine on that tag runs only for its mail. Forms a Bot asks you to fill in can arrive with known fields filled in, and you can edit them before you submit. While a paid account merge is still moving this account's data, Settings shows Your accounts are being merged, with Contact Support if it runs long. Team admins can turn off Messaging between Bots under Bot capabilities on the dashboard, so members' Bots can't message or hand work to other Bots. Teams Enterprise team admins can recreate, terminate, or delete members' Grok Bot computers from Manage Bot Computers on the dashboard or through the Admin API. Enterprise When a Bot's computer runs low on disk, the Bot tells you once, names the biggest files, and deletes them only if you agree. Improved While you use Grok Bot on a Mac or Windows PC, Bot replies and questions notify you there instead of your phone. 0.70.2+ Requires Grok Bot 0.70.2 or later You can attach files up to 250 MB and videos up to 1 GB, and the Bot says when a video is too large to watch. 0.70.2+ Requires Grok Bot 0.70.2 or later One message can carry up to 20 attachments instead of 6, and a notice says how many weren't added past the 200 MB total. Images a Bot creates or captures, and files from cloud agents it started, load in the chat while its computer is asleep. If a voice chat's connection drops, the call reconnects and continues the same conversation instead of ending. Bots can use up to 200 skills from your installed plugins instead of 24, so skills from plugins you add are no longer left out. When a Bot's computer is asleep, clicking the Computer is asleep preview wakes it in place, replacing the separate Wake button. Grok Bot opens while the Bot's computer is still starting, instead of waiting behind a full-window Setting up Grok Bot's computer screen. Sending while the Bot's computer wakes no longer shows Waiting to send… under your message or Waking your computer… in the message box. Bots can archive, move, delete, flag, or mark many Outlook messages as read or unread in one step instead of one at a time. At checkout, Bots use card details or photos you send in chat, asking only for missing fields or a verification code in a Secure Form. When GitHub can't see a repository, the Bot stops retrying and gives you a link to the GitHub page where you grant access. Bot searches on X with date limits, minimum likes or reposts, or filters X doesn't support now return posts instead of being rejected. When a Bot asks you to choose with a question card, it no longer repeats the question and options in a message beside it. Email drafts from a Bot's own address show attachments as file cards, marked when they can't be sent, changed since attached, are too large, or weren't scanned. Merging accounts finishes when both accounts have files on the Bot's computer, keeping both sets and adding (from transferred account) to clashing file names. In Team Bot Slack setup, Connect goes straight to Slack, Awaiting admin approval offers Resubmit, and a denied request shows when it was denied. Teams When a Team Bot asks to use your connected account, the card explains the access covers only your own messages and others can't use it. Teams Captions in the full-screen image viewer show formatting and clickable links, and images keep their size as you page between them. In a Bot's info pane, the name reads as plain text until you hover or click to rename it, and screen readers announce it as editable. On approval cards, the rule under labels such as Paused by your Ask first rule shows as plain text, without a box or quotation marks. Animated Bot avatars in the sidebar and a chat's activity line move more smoothly. When GitHub isn't connected, the Bot offers a single Connect GitHub action instead of listing every GitHub tool. A voice call from your phone wakes the Bot's sleeping computer, so the Bot can work with what you said after the call. Fixed While the Bot's computer is asleep, Grok Bot keeps what it loaded and says Your computer is asleep instead of showing Couldn't refresh or connection errors. When the Bot's computer updates, a working Bot reconnects to the new computer and keeps going. When the Bot's computer fails to wake, the Bot says it couldn't start instead of retrying as if it were still starting up. Images and files a Bot shares from its computer still load in the chat when the app can't fetch them from that computer directly. Opening a file right after you send it shows its contents instead of File unavailable. When the server fails an attachment upload, Grok Bot says Couldn't upload an attachment and keeps your draft, instead of asking you to check your connection. When your computer sleeps, Bots treat it as disconnected within two minutes and say so right away, instead of waiting for commands to time out. After a Wi-Fi, VPN, or other network change, Bots can run tasks on your computer right away instead of finding it unreachable. Commands a Bot runs on your computer keep going through brief connection stalls and long waits instead of failing as temporarily unreachable. If work is meant for one of your computers that's offline, the Bot tells you instead of running it on another computer without asking. Background jobs a Bot starts on your Mac, such as a local server, keep running after the command returns. Plugin and Auto-review settings changes keep reaching the Bot's computer after Grok Bot reconnects, instead of stalling until a restart. When a Bot asks to wait on a command longer than the time limit, it's told the limit right away instead of timing out. When a safety check blocks a Bot's reply, the chat shows Blocked by a safety check and Try a different message instead of a generic error. Tables in Bot replies stay within the reply's width and scroll sideways when they need more room. Attachments in one message that share a file name are numbered, such as report.pdf (2), so you can open or remove the right one. On Windows, pasting text copied from a list into the message box keeps it inline instead of splitting it into extra paragraphs. On Windows and Linux, text copied from a chat pastes into other apps with non-English characters and curly quotes intact. Opening Grok Bot to a restored chat no longer flashes a Couldn't refresh bar above the message box. Switching accounts or signing back in shows the app's loading frame instead of a blank white window. Switching accounts while a queued message is canceled or refused no longer puts its text and attachments in the other account's message box. Accounts without Grok Bot access finish setup and see just the access notice, without setup or load errors. When the Bot you had open is deleted on another device, Grok Bot opens another of your Bots instead of an empty pane. Deleting several Bots at once still deletes the rest when one fails, and the alert names only the Bot that failed. Sidebar section changes that can't be saved stay put with Can't reach your computer and Retry, then save once your computer is reachable. In the collapsed sidebar, a Bot list that can't load shows a warning icon with retry instead of text squeezed letter by letter. The full-screen computer view no longer shows a cut-off snippet of a subagent's instructions or a Couldn't load subagents line. When a Bot's routines fail to load, Couldn't load routines appears inside the Routines section of its details pane. With the details pane open and no Bot selected, a failed primary Bot load shows Couldn't load and Try again. When a Bot's skills can't be loaded, the @ menu no longer shows a Couldn't load skills row. The sidebar's number shortcut badges no longer stay on screen after you change zoom with Cmd or Ctrl. In the collapsed sidebar, the More unreads button is a circle with its arrow centered. When you drag Bots or sections in the sidebar, screen readers announce their names and where they land. Screen readers announce a Bot's reply even when it arrives after the announcement that the Bot stopped. When you Tab to a link and its preview card opens, keyboard focus moves into the card. When a Bot changes a routine while the app is briefly disconnected, the Routines list updates once it reconnects, without a reload. After onboarding creates your primary Bot, the Introducing your primary Bot chooser no longer asks you to pick one again. After you answer a request to use your computer, the Bot's sidebar row shows Allowed, Denied, or Expired instead of Permission required. When you pause and keep talking in a voice chat, the transcript extends your line instead of repeating it, and leaves out noise tags. Connector calls no longer time out after one minute: they wait up to two minutes for a reply, and longer while the connector reports progress. Bots see the full parameters of tools on connectors from Grok, so they call those tools correctly instead of guessing. Bots hit X's rate limit less often when searching X or reading posts, and a rate-limited call no longer counts toward your X read limit. Bots work with a specific Stripe customer, invoice, subscription, or payment on the first try instead of hitting a missing parameter error. Stop also ends a Bot's background subagents, so their results no longer wake the Bot afterward, and their pending approval cards expire. When you hand the Bot's computer back with I'm done or Skip, the Bot posts its answer in the chat instead of sometimes staying silent. Scripts a Bot runs in its browser no longer fail over extra or out-of-range settings, so browser tasks finish more often. Secure Form fills fields on more websites, including inside embedded frames from other sites, instead of leaving them empty. When a routine needs to sign in to a site, it asks you in chat at that step instead of quietly stopping. Bots ask for logins and other multi-field details on one Secure Form instead of a secret request card that holds a single value. Screenshot, computer, and browser actions keep working when you haven't connected 1Password, instead of failing on a saved-login check. Messaging from another time zone updates the zone the Bot uses for schedules and reminders right away, unless you chose one under Timezone in Settings. Bots with any shape the avatar editor offers, such as sparkle or star, can be shared as templates without the Bot changing its look. Emails that arrive in a Bot's own inbox keep each link's web address, so the Bot can open verification and sign-in links. Email sent to a Bot's own address arrives even when its subject, sender address, or thread references are very long. After you choose Disable drafts for a Bot, it sends email from its own address right away, without a draft card. After a Bot claims an email address, opening Email or Plugins shows it as Connected instead of still offering Connect. When you allow a Team Bot to use one of your plugins, its tools work right away instead of the Bot failing to find them. Teams Plugins on a Team Bot use the settings your team admin entered, such as a Datadog site, when the Bot has none of its own. Teams A Team Bot still named New team bot with no description shows Draft, not Published to your team, until you rename it or add a description. Teams Grok Bot works under your selected team even when another team you're on uses Privacy Mode (Legacy), as long as the selected team doesn't. Account merges that move many Bots finish in one go instead of failing and showing Your account merge is taking longer than usual. When a downloaded update is withdrawn, Restart to Update goes away and Grok Bot keeps your current version, even when you quit on a Mac. An update download that keeps restarting from the beginning waits between tries and then stops with an error instead of retrying nonstop. When the update server sends a broken response, Settings says The update server returned an invalid response instead of blaming your connection. Restart to Update shows Restarting… and waits up to two minutes for commands a Bot is running on your computer to finish. When an update replaces Grok Bot's files while it runs, reloading or crash recovery relaunches the app instead of showing a blank window. On Linux deb and rpm installs, Update required links the latest package, leading with it when the package repository doesn't have the update yet. On Windows and Linux, opening Grok Bot while it's still quitting reopens it after the quit instead of leaving nothing open. GitHub tools stay available after a connection block and work once you reconnect, without starting a new chat. When Gmail refuses to open a full thread, the Bot still answers from the thread's first message. A connector that still needs Allow keeps its name, so the Bot asks you to allow it instead of saying it can't find it. A Bot keeps its connector tools while its computer is asleep, starting up, or not created yet, instead of losing them for that turn.

item.title: Bot email addresses, X search, and in-chat apps (0.70.2)
item.description: New Bots can claim their own email address and receive mail there, and email they send from it waits for your approval on a draft card. Bots can search X and read posts and profiles without you connecting an X account. Connectors that come with an app, such as Figma, Notion, and Canva, can show it as an interactive card in the chat. Bots can pay with X Money or Stripe Link. Bots can find a Bot template that fits what you describe and link it in the chat. On Mac, View Unread in the View menu shows only Bots with unread messages in the sidebar. Press Cmd+F or Ctrl+F on an open page to search it in a Find in page bar. You can rename a page from its title, and the new name shows everywhere. Shared pages have a title bar with Download, which saves a PDF, plus Try Grok Bot for visitors and Share for the owner. Adding Glean asks for your Glean MCP URL and connects it after you sign in to Glean in your browser. QuickBooks Online is available to connect. Bots can save a web page as a PDF from their browser and send audio files such as MP3, M4A, and WAV. The full-screen video player has a speed menu, and voice calls offer 0.5x speed. Teammates can approve Auto-review requests, including Always allow, from their own direct message with a Team Bot. Teams Improved Before an action it can't undo, such as sending, posting, buying, or deleting, a Bot checks your own messages for approval. Browser approval cards describe actions in plain words, such as Open a new tab in Grok Bot's browser, and a saved Allow rule applies the same way on every tool. When more than one account could send an email, the Bot asks which address to use, then tells you the address it sent from. When a sign-in emails a code or link, the Bot reads it from your connected Gmail or Outlook, or its own inbox, instead of asking you. After a bank or brokerage connector returns data, the Bot asks before sharing it anywhere else. Bots acknowledge your message before they start longer work. Reactions sit on the message bubble, the quick row includes your recent emoji, and each person shows only their latest reaction. Reply quotes show the quoted text and jump to the replied message when clicked, and selecting text shows an Add to chat pill. While a Bot works with nothing to report, a 1:1 chat shows just its animated avatar. While attachments upload, your message shows a Sending… bar that fills as the files upload. The full-screen computer view opens in Watching until you press Take control. When a Bot's computer is asleep, the Computer tab shows a Wake button that wakes it in place. Computer settings separate Your computer from the Bot's computer, and Updates shows only app updates. Updates to Grok Bot's computer run without status pills in the sidebar; you see a notice only if one leaves the computer unreachable. After saving a routine, the Bot sums up what it does and who receives the result, and each run delivers there. When you give a Bot a connector link, it installs the matching plugin from the catalog when there is one. Connect Apps lists the most-installed plugins first, search also finds plugins whose description matches, and a search with no results says so. Bots can wait for a background command on their computer to finish, shown as Waiting on results. When GitHub refuses a repository or Vercel a team, the Bot suggests ones it can reach or asks you to reconnect. Adding an MCP server on a private Tailscale network now explains that Grok Bot can't reach it yet and suggests exposing it with Tailscale Funnel. Canvases and documents are both labeled Page. Typing # in the composer no longer opens the pull request picker. Fixed Connector calls fail less often: Bots fix wrongly shaped arguments and accept Notion links and Slack channel names before sending. When a connector rate-limits your account, Bots wait for the retry delay instead of calling it in a loop. With 1Password connected, browser and computer actions retry through brief connection errors instead of stopping. Slack, Gmail, and Outlook drafts retry through temporary rate limits and say if they still couldn't send. Slack messages a Bot drafts no longer turn into one raw code block when sent. Gmail drafts use your default send-as address and add your own signature, not one quoted from someone else. Bot emails with non-English names or subjects no longer bounce, replies to them stay in the same thread, and small images in incoming mail are kept. When Agent email is off for your team or account, the Bot says so instead of calling it a temporary problem. Files and images Bots send from their computer arrive in the chat, ahead of any question card. Opening a file while the Bot's computer is asleep wakes it and opens the file. When chats, pages, skills, routines, or plugins fail to load, the app shows the error with Try again and keeps what it last loaded. Search finds message text and attachment names in all chats, including the open one. The open chat is marked read when you relaunch the app, come back to your computer, or click its row again. While a Bot searches the web or reads pages, the chat and Slack show what it's doing, such as Digging around, instead of Working in Cursor. The Bot's browser keeps downloads under their own file names and starts again after its profile folder is removed. Outlook shows its Authorize card when a change needs more permission, and Bots stop retrying on deleted or protected items. All-day calendar events stay on the right date, and Bots check your other calendars before saying an event is missing. Plugins installed from chat or the web are ready on the Bot's computer, and local plugins such as Xero get the settings you entered. Long messages show Show more right away, so opening a chat no longer jumps. Publishing, sharing, or deleting a Bot, and adding one from a template, work while its computer is asleep or unreachable. Switching chats or focusing the window no longer wakes a sleeping computer. Switching accounts lands on the new account within seconds, even when another computer is asleep. Pinned Bots stay in sync between the desktop and the phone. If the window keeps crashing, Grok Bot offers to reload it or quit, and a window left blank after an update relaunches. Bots no longer sign you out of a connector while repairing it, and a connector account you sign out of stays signed out. When a model isn't available in your region, the turn stops and explains why, and Bots fall back to Grok. In Slack, Bots answer messages whose thread they can't read, and asking a teammate's Bot no longer adds it to your sidebar. Connecting Slack from the dashboard on grok.com now brings you back there to finish linking your Slack account. In voice calls, the Bot knows today's date in your time zone instead of sometimes using tomorrow's. On Linux, the app stays responsive and can quit while a notification is showing. Usage & Billing shows your plan name on Current plan, and the usage meter labels its percentage as used.

item.title: Slide decks and Bot-colored chats (0.68.1)
item.description: New Your messages in a 1:1 Bot chat take that Bot's color; set Accent to Black in Settings → General to turn it off. 0.64.0+ Requires Grok Bot 0.64.0 or later Bots can build slide decks with you, showing sample slides to choose from, and deliver them as PowerPoint files or Google Slides. Bots can send formatted emails from a draft card, so recipients see headings, bold text, and lists. Bots can search your Gmail Spam folder and move a message back to your inbox. Team Bots can mention a Slack user group so its members get notified, while @here and @channel still don't ping anyone. Teams Improved Typing / in the composer no longer opens a menu of skills and actions. Bots work faster on their computer: actions settle sooner, screenshots come back quicker, and new windows skip a five-second wait. The Bot's computer has a 1920 × 1200 screen, up from 1280 × 800, giving more room when you watch it or take over. item.title: Onboarding, team invites, and HTML previews (0.31.0)
item.description: New Onboarding asks what you'll be working on most and suggests Bots for that kind of work. Team admins can invite their whole team to Grok Bot, or pick specific groups and members. Teams A Setup Checklist on the dashboard walks admins through plugins, Slack, GitHub, sign-in, and inviting teammates. Teams Opening an HTML file your Bot made shows a preview, with Source for the code, and links in it open in your browser. A Cloud Agent's open button lets you choose Open in Web or Open in Cursor, and remembers your choice. When a firewall or VPN blocks your Bot's computer, Grok Bot says it can't reach it and offers Retry. Improved You can create more than 50 Bots. Hourly, interval, and daily routines run on a schedule counted from when you create them. Fixed Files you attach and dictation stay with the Bot you started them in, even if you switch Bots. A Cloud Agent your Bot started isn't launched twice when a launch is retried, and your Bot hears when it finishes. On Linux, links that open Grok Bot launch the app. Images you attach show thumbnails on Windows.

item.title: Template sharing, Link purchases, and languages (0.30.0)
item.description: New Share a Bot as a template: choose whether your team or anyone can use it, and others add their own copy from the link. When your Bot wants to buy something, a card shows the amount for you to Allow or Deny, then Link completes the payment. Team admins choose whether members can share templates publicly or only within the team. Teams Action Recording on the dashboard records members' Grok Bot actions to your team's audit log. Enterprise Grok Bot is available in Arabic, Ukrainian, Dutch, Greek, Afrikaans, and Hebrew, with right-to-left layouts for Arabic and Hebrew. Command-Shift-V, or Ctrl-Shift-V, pastes text into the message box without formatting. You can approve a task on one computer from another computer where you're signed in. Enterprise usage settings show a Personal Usage chart of your spend against last month and your limit. Enterprise Improved Jump to lists matching Bots above actions and messages. Send Feedback lets you ask for a response. Fixed Pasting an image attaches it as a file, and the cursor stays in view after you paste a long message. Your Bot's browser switches to the tab it picks and reloads pages that fail to open.

item.title: Computers in Settings and phone replies (0.29.0)
item.description: New Settings has a Computer section listing your computers, where you choose Always allow, Ask every time, or Never allow for actions on each one. Notifications from the Grok app on your phone show your Bot's reply. Improved You can drag the details pane wider, up to the chat's minimum width. Fixed Your Bot's computer starts when you belong to more than one team.

item.title: Russian, Turkish, Italian, and Swedish (0.28.0)
item.description: New Grok Bot is available in Russian, Turkish, Italian, and Swedish, and follows your computer's language. Improved Settings and plugin links your Bot writes show the real name of the setting or plugin. Fixed Signing in stops waiting after five minutes, so you can try again.

item.title: Pro and SuperGrok access, and webhook data (0.27.0)
item.description: New Cursor Pro subscribers can now use Grok Bot, as can SuperGrok and X Premium+ subscribers who link their account. Improved Admin setup on the dashboard shows Enabled once your team finishes setting up Grok Bot. Teams Routines started by a webhook receive the request body, so your Bot can act on what was sent. Fixed If a chat can't load, Grok Bot says so and offers Retry.

item.title: App menu, right-to-left typing, and updates (0.26.0)
item.description: New The app menu has Settings…, Check for Updates, and Restart to Update when an update is ready. Improved Typing in Arabic, Hebrew, and other right-to-left languages starts on the right, and replies that mix directions lay out each paragraph correctly. Unread Bots appear first in the search palette. Update Grok Bot's Computer explains when an update only touches the software your Bots run on, so installed apps stay. Fixed Grok Bot uses the team you picked at sign-in the first time it loads your teams. Alerts, feedback, and About open on top of Settings. When an update is required, the Update required screen covers the whole window.

item.title: Multi-select questions and on-demand limits (0.25.0)
item.description: New When your Bot asks a question that allows several answers, select the ones you want and press Submit. On an individual plan, set your monthly on-demand limit to None, Fixed, or Unlimited in Usage & Billing. A GitHub routine can watch a single pull request, including when it closes, and removes itself once the pull request merges or closes. Download a diagram in the chat as a PNG image. Click a Bot mentioned in a conversation to open it. Improved When your included usage runs out, team members can upgrade to a Premium seat, alongside Ultra and SuperGrok Heavy. A Bot you delete disappears from the sidebar as soon as you confirm, and you're told if deleting fails. Fixed Text you paste into the message box stays plain, and anything you type right after sending is kept. Messages that start with a link show the rest of their text, and the link stays clickable. Grok Bot uses the team you selected for rules, Usage & Billing, and Computers, and switches to a team you can still use if yours is gone. Privacy Mode keeps a conversation off your Bot's computer when it must not be stored. Your Bot's computer finishes restoring its files, including ones with long names.

item.title: Setting links, team sign-in, and voice input (0.24.0)
item.description: New Hover a settings or plugin title and choose Copy link to share a direct link to it. Right-click a video and choose Save video… to keep it. If you belong to more than one team, sign-in asks you to pick one. Onboarding and the access screen show the email you're signed in with, with Log out. Improved Voice input detects the language you speak instead of assuming your app or system language. Sign out explains that it removes the account and its local data from this computer, and your Bots and chats return when you sign in again. Fixed Today and Yesterday update after midnight, and attachments stay on the day you sent them. Links into Grok Bot open the right page instead of only bringing the window forward. If you message your Bot while a routine is running, the routine runs again afterward.

item.title: Team setup and translation fixes (0.22.0)
item.description: Fixed Setting up Grok Bot on the dashboard uses the team you selected. Teams Spanish and French translations of plugin counts, routine schedules, and alert statuses read correctly.

item.title: App languages, emoji, and webhook routines (0.21.0)
item.description: New Pick the app's language under Appearance, including Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hindi, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, and Polish. Type : in the message box to pick an emoji, or finish a short name with : to insert it. Routines can start from a webhook, with their own Webhook URL and Webhook key. Download an attachment from the message menu, or use Download all when a message has several. Enterprise admins can save Team Setup scripts on the dashboard that run on every member's Bot computer. Enterprise Enterprise admins can set a network access policy for their team's Bots from the dashboard. Enterprise Improved Dictation follows your system language, and Enter stops a recording. Updating or recreating your Bot's computer explains that files and logins stay while installed apps and packages are removed. Plugins opens with your plugins, category filters, and a Team Plugins section. Fixed Files search finds files on your Bot's computer, and says Search unavailable when it can't run. Grok Bot reconnects to your computer after sleep or a dropped connection, so actions on it keep working. When your sign-in expires, Grok Bot asks you to sign in again.

item.title: Dictation, formatting, and clearer errors (0.20.0)
item.description: New Press or hold ⌘D (Ctrl+D on Windows and Linux) to dictate into the message field, and Send message sends the transcript as soon as it's ready. Rename a plugin's default account with Edit default account. Improved Your Bot's computer can hold Shift, Ctrl, Alt, or Command while it clicks, drags, and scrolls. When a reply fails, Grok Bot explains what happened in plain language. Your Bot cancels, archives, and unarchives Cloud Agents as soon as you ask. Fixed Replies show underline, subscript, superscript, and highlight formatting.

item.title: Manage Plan, scrolling, and Bot naming (0.19.0)
item.description: New Settings has Manage Plan, showing the upgrade options for your account. When your included usage runs out, you can upgrade to Ultra or link a SuperGrok Heavy subscription. A Scroll to bottom button appears above the message field when you scroll up. Settings has Use hardware acceleration under General → System, on by default on a Mac, with Restart to Apply. Improved Settings, search, and confirmations say Bot instead of Agent. The message field stays at the bottom of the chat, even when the chat is empty. Start a computer update from Settings with Update Grok Bot's Computer. Requests to run a command on your computer hide the command until you choose Show the command. Fixed Help Center opens the Grok Bot docs. ⌘V pastes into a terminal on your Bot's computer. Allow, Never, and Deny now clear a stuck request to run commands on your computer.

item.title: Cancel Trial in Usage & Billing (0.18.0)
item.description: New You can end a free trial early with Cancel Trial in Usage & Billing, which removes any remaining trial credits.

item.title: More routine triggers and pull request links (0.17.0)
item.description: New Members with a Standard seat on a self-serve team can use Grok Bot through a linked SuperGrok Heavy subscription. Teams Improved Your Bot can create routines that start from a Microsoft Teams message, a Linear issue, a Sentry alert, or a PagerDuty incident. Auto-review asks before your Bot runs a task you didn't ask for. Pull request links open where you or your team chose, or on GitHub if neither has chosen. Fixed The account row in the sidebar opens the account menu, even during setup. Your Bot stops showing that it's working once a background task finishes. A connector that stops responding times out after three minutes, so your Bot can carry on. Update Grok Bot's Computer finishes and keeps file permissions and shortcuts. Choosing a shape or color keeps a picture you added until you press Set avatar.
